rounds.name: The Cardboard Arcade
rounds.situation: At the school fair, you walk past a game made from an old cardboard box. You think it looks boring. Then a classmate tilts the box, and a marble rolls through a clever maze.
rounds.discussion: Would your ending change what you do next? Explain using one detail from the fair.
rounds.traditionalMeaning: Find out what something is really like before judging it by its appearance.

rounds.name: The Book Drive
rounds.situation: Two boxes of books need to go into the library before lunch. They’re too heavy for you to carry alone. Three classmates have just arrived.
rounds.discussion: What would you ask your classmates to do? Explain how your ending helps or where it falls short.
rounds.traditionalMeaning: A job is easier when people share the work.

rounds.name: The Greenhouse Door
rounds.opener: I was about to leave when I noticed …
rounds.situation: While watering plants in the school greenhouse, you spot a tiny door at the base of a flowerpot. A trail of muddy footprints leads away from it.
rounds.discussion: Read your ending aloud. Which detail might turn it into the start of a mystery? If it clashes with the scene, explain why.

rounds.name: The Trophy Case Duck
rounds.opener: I should have left it where it was, but …
rounds.situation: You find a rubber duck under the school trophy case. You’ve seen four more today, and each one was somewhere you went with your friend yesterday.
rounds.discussion: What does your finished line suggest you do with the duck? Explain what the places you found the ducks might tell you.

rounds.name: The Wrong Group Chat
rounds.opener: The first thing I said was …
rounds.situation: You sent a message about a surprise for your friend to the class group chat. Your friend is in that chat. They’re sitting next to you and just picked up their phone.
rounds.discussion: How would your friend respond to your line? Use one detail to explain your prediction.

rounds.name: The Last Window Seat
rounds.opener: I looked at the empty seat and said …
rounds.situation: There’s one window seat left on the bus. You wanted it all morning. A classmate behind you says looking out the window helps when they feel sick on the bus.
rounds.discussion: Whose needs does your line address? Use one detail from the bus scene to explain how it fits or misses the moment.

rounds.name: Tortoise on the Move
rounds.opener: If you’re near the library, please …
rounds.situation: The science room’s pet tortoise is slowly crossing the hallway toward the library. The bell has just rung, and students are about to come out of class.
rounds.discussion: What would students do if they heard your announcement? Which detail about the hallway should they know?
